system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: the inputs for the selection agent include previous selected indexes, column candidates to select from, total storage budget, and the storage budget already used
system_prompt_style.note: Per-agent prompts filled with workload/budget variables; no prompt text published.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: our approach extracts only index-relevant information and reorganizes it at the column level, merging all workload details associated with each database column to construct a compact set of indexable candidates
env_context_strategy.note: Closest value: a compact schema/column-candidate summary is injected up front; no agent navigation tools.

context_compaction.note: No compaction mechanism described; workload representation reduces input size but is not history compaction.

observation_format.evidence_quote: We design a novel textual workload representation that transforms the complex index recom-mendation problem into an LLM-compatible format.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: New Action: Selection Agent New Index Selection: [lineitem(l_orderkey)]
tool_call_format.note: Agents emit structured textual action names/index lists; no tool-calling API described.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: the index advisor problem seeks to automatically identify an optimal set of indexes
edit_primitive.note: No file editing; output is an index configuration.

protocol_standardization.note: Agents are direct function calls; no protocol mentioned.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: At the beginning of each sub-step, the planning agent determines the next action in line 7.
loop_primitives.note: Planner chooses an action each iteration; reflection feeds back.

planning_granularity.note: A stored planning path of actions re-read by the reflection agent.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a hierarchical multi-agent based index recommendation pipeline
multi_agent_topology.note: High-level planning/reflection agents direct low-level selection/combination/revision agents.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: it outputs an action for the current sub-step: ‘Selection’, ‘Combination’, or ‘Revision’, each invoking a corresponding low-level agent

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Output the final index selection𝐼 𝑎
human_in_loop.note: Loop runs to completion with no human gate.

short_term_state.note: State = current index set, budget used, action path.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: AMAZe, a zero-shot LLM-based index advisor with a multi-agent framework
long_term_memory.note: Static external knowledge/expert rules are given in prompts, not cross-run memory.

state_persistence.note: Runs start from scratch; no resume path described.

self_verification.evidence_quote: a reflection agent is introduced to evaluate the current path, with the goal of identifying and correcting errors
self_verification.note: Revision agent plus a trained MLP regression indicator (non-LLM verifier) also checks selections.

retry_policy.note: Iterative refinement inside one run; no task-level re-attempt.

rollback.evidence_quote: the revision agent ensures effectiveness by removing such cases once called in line 16
rollback.note: Index removal is an edit, not a state rollback mechanism.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: we introduce a hyperparameter𝛼, which defines the maximum number of planning sub-steps
termination_condition.note: Also 'Stop' action from the planning agent.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: The average num-ber of input tokens and the corresponding API cost for AMAZe and LLMIdxAdvis are recorded in Table 5.
cost_controls.note: Cost measured but no budget/caching/routing mechanism; storage budget is a task constraint, not an LLM cost control.

timeouts.note: Only an iteration cap; no timeout reported.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: We choose the popular DBMS Post-greSQL 14.2 to evaluate all the queries
execution_isolation.note: Actions are executed against a DBMS (hypothetical index / cost estimation), not a sandboxed shell; closest value chosen.

network_policy.evidence_quote: We leverage the GPT-4o-0806 [ 5] version within the OpenAI API as the default LLM backbone for the agents.
network_policy.note: No network restriction described; external API used.

permission_model.evidence_quote: each invoking a corresponding low-level agent
permission_model.note: Actions execute directly; only an exception is recorded for undefined agent calls.

tracing.evidence_quote: An example of AMAZe’s planning steps and index recommendation on TPC-H 20% budget can be found in Figure 6.
tracing.note: Per-step action/index/budget record shown; not stated as a persisted trace format.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: We reproduce all the heuristic-based baselines based on the evaluation work [17].
eval_hooks.note: No repo released; evaluation uses external benchmark harness.

guardrails.evidence_quote: a hallucination check will be conducted in the revision agent to identify and correct the wrong or non-existing index selections
guardrails.note: Revision agent filters hallucinated/regressive outputs before final recommendation.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Index recommendation is one of the most important problems in database management system (DBMS) optimization.

open_source.evidence_quote: AMAZe: A Multi-Agent Zero-shot Index Advisor for Relational Databases
open_source.note: No repository URL or license given in the paper.
